draft.title: A significant person in Hinduism
card: A significant person in a religion is someone whose teaching and life changed how followers think and act. In Hinduism, two such figures are Shankara and Mahatma Gandhi.
A teacher who lived in India around the 8th century CE. He taught Advaita Vedanta, the view that the individual self (atman) and ultimate reality (Brahman) are one.
A leader (1869 to 1948) in India's struggle for independence from British rule. He drew on Hindu ideas such as ahimsa (non-violence) and satya (truth) to shape his way of acting in public life.

Shankara influenced Hindu thought through his writing, his commentaries on sacred texts and his debates. Gandhi influenced Hindu practice by showing how beliefs could guide action in daily and political life.
draft.remember: Shankara shaped Hindu thought through teaching. Gandhi showed Hindu ideas in action.

a.q: Which statement best describes Shankara's influence on Hinduism?
opts: He taught that the self and Brahman are one
He led non-violent protest against British rule
He taught that the self and Brahman are always separate
He founded a new religion that replaced Vedic teachings
a.why: Shankara taught Advaita Vedanta, which holds that atman and Brahman are one. Leading non-violent protest describes Gandhi, not Shankara, and that is the most tempting mix-up.
a.clue: Think of the teacher of Advaita Vedanta.

b.q: A student says Gandhi was significant in Hinduism because he turned the idea of ahimsa into public action. Which reason best supports this?
opts: He applied non-violence and truth to political struggle
He wrote commentaries explaining that atman is Brahman
He taught that political life should be left to others
He taught that non-violence belongs only in temple worship
b.why: Gandhi drew on ahimsa and satya to guide how he acted in the independence struggle, so his influence was on practice. Writing commentaries on atman and Brahman describes Shankara, so it supports a different kind of influence.
b.clue: Gandhi's influence was seen in what he did, not in philosophical commentary.

a.best: He taught that the self and Brahman are one

b.best: He applied non-violence and truth to political struggle

b.q: A Hindu youth group in Parramatta marches for fair pay for workers. Members agree to speak honestly and never hit back if insulted. Whose influence does this reflect most closely, and why?
opts: Gandhi, as he showed how ahimsa could guide public action
Shankara, as he taught that atman and Brahman are one
Shankara, as he led India's struggle for independence
Gandhi, as he taught Advaita Vedanta in the 8th century
